title: Cabaret work at Mammy Louise's Creole Garden in Cleveland
summary: The reed section joins Chester Clark's band with Harry Edison, earning small pay with one meal a day and playing all night for cabaret dancers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Disbanded. A musician friend of ours who formerly played with the Alphonso Trent band was living in Cleveland and he had a band working at Mammy Louise's Creole Garden, in Cleveland, Ohio. We had contacted him and he kept the job open for our reed section. Which was my partner Jeter and my brother Charles Pillars and myself. So we left Albany, New York and drove into Cleveland and we arrived in Cleveland a couple of days late, but we had a rehearsal and found out in this particular band was one of our former drummers, Godley Cartier, was -- and a little kid named Harry Edison -- Harry was 16 or 17 years old. Chester Lane played trumpet --

I mean Chester Clark played trumpet and his wife, played the piano, can't think of her name right now. But she was a very fine musician. We found out that our salary was between $6.00 and $9.00 a week, and we'd get one meal a day, which was dinner -- dinner meal, and we went to work at 9:00 o'clock at night and played until everybody went

home the following morning. So, we opened up with Chester Clark. They had dancers back in those days, cabaret dancers, and the dancers would sing to each table, before coming back on the floor and singing their last chorus. And they would keep the money, tips, rather, that they made in their hands and when they finished singing the would bring the money up to the bandleader and put it into a kitty.
